Ghanaśyāma

Ghanaśyāma
alias Cauṇḍāji Panth; versatile an. arrogant writer from Mahārāṣṭra who lived in Tanjore a. a minister of king Tukkojī I (1729-35 A. D.); also called Āryaka (See MD. 12519); an. had the titles Sarvajñakavi, Vaśyavacas, Kaṇṭhīrava an. Sarasvatī; born in January 1706 (on his horoscope see JOR. Madras IV. p.. 71-77); son of Kāśī an. Mahādeva (father's name is not Kāśīmahādeva a. given on the basis of col. Kāśīmahā- [Page274-a. devasūnu, MT. 1352; see Intro. to C. on Campūrāmāyaṇa, TD. 4143 yasyezo 'grabhavaH pitA kila mahAdevaH sa kAzIprasaH; delete the entry Kāśīmahādeva from NCC. IV. p. 135b); grandson of Cauṇḍabālāji of Mauna Bhārgava family (his mother's father being Timmāji Bālāji of Kauṇḍinyagotra); younger brother of Īśa (who became a. ascetic assuming the name Cidambara Brahman who settled in Devīpaṭṭana near Navapāṣāṇa); had two wives Sundarī an. Kamalā (joint a.s of C. on Viddhasālabhañjikā, TD. 4678), an. a sister Śākambharī; father of Candraśekhara (a. of C. on Ghanaśyāma's Ḍamaruka an. Pracaṇḍarāhūdaya) an. Govardhana (blind from birth an. a. of C. on Ghaṭakarpara, see above); in C. on Nīlakaṇṭhavijaya he says he composed 64 works in Skt., 20 in Pkt. an. 25 in vernaculars; his wives give a long list of his works in the beg. of their C. on Viddhasālabhañjikā, TD. 4678.
On his life an. works see V. A. Ramaswami Sastri, JOR. Madras III. p.. 231-43; also Y. Mahalinga Sastri, JOR. Madras IV. p.. 71-77 an. A. N. Upadhye, Prof. M. Hiriyanna Com. Vol. p.. 216-20.
